definitions.gloss: by far; far more; much; considerably
definitions.explanation: Used before comparatives to emphasize a large degree of difference between two things.

examples.japanese: こちらのほうがはるかに{安|やす}い。
{今年|ことし}の{夏|なつ}は{去年|きょねん}よりはるかに{暑|あつ}い。
examples.english: This summer is much hotter than last year.

examples.japanese: {実際|じっさい}にやってみると、{想像|そうぞう}していたよりはるかに{難|むずか}しかった。
examples.english: When I actually tried it, it was far more difficult than I had imagined.

notes:
An adverb used to emphasize a significant degree of difference in comparisons. It always modifies a comparative expression — typically an adjective or adverb used with より. It can also be written in kanji as {遥|はる}かに, though the hiragana form is more common in modern writing.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- AはBよりはるかに〜: A is far more ~ than B
- {想像|そうぞう}よりはるかに: far more than imagined
- {予想|よそう}よりはるかに: far more than expected

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ずっと: much; by far — slightly more casual, used in the same comparative patterns
- {遥|はる}か: far; distant — the base adjective form, used for spatial or temporal distance (e.g., はるか{昔|むかし} "long, long ago")
- だいぶ: considerably — indicates a notable degree but weaker emphasis than はるかに
